newsitem.title: UK: Bulgaria and Russia outperform rising Brady market.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria and Russia outperform rising Brady market.

text.p: The tone in the Brady bond market remained positive on Monday on the back of rising U.S. Treasuries with Bulgarian and Russian debt particularly strong, bankers said.
The Treasury market rallied late last week following the release of soft economic data which boosted expectations that U.S. interest rates would be steady for the time being.
"The whole (Brady) market has profited from the rise in Treasuries, but Bulgaria and Russia have outperformed the market quite handsomely," an emerging market economist at a U.S. bank said.
Bulgarian FRBs were up 0.875 points at 57/57.625 cents in the dollar. The biggest rise in Russian paper was in series six MinFins, up 0.625 points at 54.125/54.375 cents.
Bankers said there was no particular catalyst for the strong performance of Russia and Bulgaria, but reflected the positive fundamentals in both countries.

"In Russia, (first deputy prime minister Anatoly) Chubais' attempts to push through the budget and the expectations that a closing date for the London Club deal will be set in July is buoying demand," a trader at a European bank said.
"Similarly, Bulgaria is seen to have ever-improving fundamentals," he said.
On the Latin American side, traders said Ecuador and Venezuela were the best performers.
"Despite the focus by the Brady market on moves in U.S. Treasuries, there is still differentiation between countries," the U.S. bank's economist said.
"Latin America is a prime example, with Ecuador and Venezuela performing much better than Brazil," he said.
In recent months emerging market debt has been heavily influenced by the direction of U.S. Treasury bonds amid expectations that rates there could go up.
"One eye will still be kept firmly on Treasuries, especially when they are volatile, but countries with positive fundamentals are being looked at more closely now," the economist said.
Analysts in New York said on Friday emerging markets were also boosted by quarter-end asset allocation, which was bringing money into the sector.
